source_intents.action_description: Log in as a Primary User with no NAV ID assigned, place an order, and inspect the order confirmation screen and Salesforce Case Queue
source_intents.expected_behavior: Order confirmation screen is displayed; a new Salesforce case is created and visible in the SF Case Queue; NAV order entry is created for the order
preconditions: No NAV ID assigned to the user
test_data_hints: Primary user account with no NAV ID
IOS SF Case in submitted state
source_intents.original_text: CF-03 | Immediate Checkout After Onboarding | Sanity | NAV ORDER ENTRY & SF Case Creation | User is a Primary, has submitted IOS case, Payment Status = Approved, no NAV assigned | 1. Login as Primary User without NAV. 2. Place an order. 3. Check confirmation screen and SF Case Queue.

source_observations.summary: Place order with qty=1 (below MOQ=2) — order ACCEPTED, MOQ check did not fire
Get order details after placement — order created, SF case ID is null (not created)

body.sf_case_error: Salesforce API timeout — case not created

reconciliation.reasoning: OBS-009 shows the order confirmation response contains sf_case_id=null and sf_case_creation_status=failed with an explicit Salesforce API timeout error. The intent states a Salesforce case MUST appear in the SF Case Queue after order placement. The NAV order entry was created (nav_order_id present) but the SF case integration is broken. This is a regression, not an intentional design change.
reconciliation.final_expected_behavior: REGRESSION DETECTED: After order placement, sf_case_id must be non-null and a case must appear in the Salesforce Case Queue. The observed system returned sf_case_id=null with sf_case_creation_status=failed. The generated test must assert that POST /rest/V1/carts/mine/payment-information followed by GET /rest/V1/orders/{id} returns a non-null sf_case_id and sf_case_creation_status=created.

classification.reasoning: Regression in an external integration (Salesforce API). API-level test is the right layer — it can assert on the sf_case_id field in the order response without requiring Salesforce sandbox access.

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: Salesforce integration is a side effect of order placement — unit tests cannot assert on the SF case creation without mocking the entire Salesforce client.
Contract testing requires a Salesforce sandbox provider; out of scope for the current demo.

dimensions.name: syntactic_validity
dimensions.notes: Syntactically valid. Correct class structure and Guzzle usage.

dimensions.name: behavior_fidelity
dimensions.notes: Correctly targets the regression: testOrderPlacementCreatesSalesforceCase asserts sf_case_id is not null, which directly probes the broken integration identified in REC-003. testOrderPlacementCreatesNavEntry adds a second axis. Missing: does not assert sf_case_creation_status = 'created', leaving the door open for a future bug where sf_case_id is populated with a stale value.

dimensions.name: coverage_delta
dimensions.notes: High-value regression coverage. Both SF case and NAV order assertions together cover the full expected post-order state. No existing tests cover this integration path.

dimensions.name: assertion_quality
dimensions.notes: assertNotNull(sf_case_id) is necessary but insufficient — does not assert that sf_case_creation_status='created'. Does not assert the SF case number format or that it is retrievable. testOrderPlacementCreatesNavEntry uses assertNotEmpty which is weaker than assertMatchesRegularExpression for a known NAV ID pattern like NAV-ORD-\d+.

dimensions.name: determinism
dimensions.notes: No randomness. Auth uses env vars. Small risk: test depends on the Salesforce integration being reachable — if SF is down, the test result is ambiguous (regression vs infrastructure failure). Consider asserting on sf_case_creation_status to distinguish these cases.

flake_signals.detail: Salesforce API returned a 503 timeout in 1 of 3 test runs — test is a flaky candidate when SF is under load.

steering_signals_applied.rule_text: Always cite source file and line number in test method docblock for traceability.
